question: what classes are you supposed to take senior year for the nursing major?

body.answer:
The catalog lists three nursing bachelor’s majors: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing RN to BSN [16]. The plans below are recommended plans for students admitted in 2023–2024, not a current-year schedule. [2][3]

**Nursing Generic BSN — Bachelor of Science in Nursing** (also published: Nursing MSN). [2]
Fourth Year, Fall Semester (total 16 credits): NURS 410 Health Issues Management II; NURS 425 Community Centered Nursing; NURS 430 Integrative Clinical Strategies III; NURS 435 Pathophysiology/Pharmacology II. [2]
Fourth Year, Spring Semester (total 16 credits): NURS 440 Integrative Clinical Strategies IV; NURS 445 Leadership in a Global World; NURS 450 Integrative Clinical Residency in Nursing; NURS 460 Clinical Management. [2]

**Nursing RN to BSN — Bachelor of Science in Nursing** (also published: Nursing MSN). [3]
Fourth Year, Fall Semester (total 16 credits): NURS 325 Nursing Research and Evidence Based Practice; NURS 460 Clinical Management; one distribution category (Culture and Creativity, Systems, Sustainability and Society, or Values and Ethics); Approved Nursing Elective. [3]
Fourth Year, Spring Semester (total 16 credits): NURS 445 Leadership in a Global World; three electives (if needed). The plan says it may differ depending on transfer credits. [3]

The provided plans do not give a senior-year schedule for the Accelerated BSN. For help confirming which track and schedule apply, contact the Nursing Programs Office: (201) 684-7749, Adler Center for Nursing Excellence 215.

question: Can you explain how general education works at Ramapo? How many gen ed credits do students need and what categories do they have to cover?

body.answer:
General Education is the broad-based foundational curriculum for undergraduates, providing context for majors, minors, and concentrations [5].

Ramapo students complete ten General Education courses: four keystone courses, one in each of four keystone categories, and one in two of three distribution categories [8]. The four keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Critical Reading & Writing 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits [8]. The keystone categories are Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits [8].

Distribution categories are Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics; take one course in two categories [8]. At least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the one housing the student's major [8]. Starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in the degree audit tools [10].

The pages do not state an exact total of required Gen Ed credits. The curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits” [6]. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all requirements [7].

Sources: [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: We're looking at the psychology major. What are the required courses, and is there a recommended order for taking them over four years?

body.answer:
Psychology BA (Bachelor of Arts) requirements [1]: Required all: PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology (4 credits; no published prerequisites [2]), PSYC 242 Statistics, and both PSYC 303 Research Methods in Psychology and PSYC 304 Data Analysis in Psychology. Select one from each: Category 1 Social and Organizational—PSYC 226 Social Psychology or PSYC 345 Workplace Psychology; Category 2 Cognition and Perception—PSYC 202 Psychology of Learning, PSYC 209 Psychology of Perception, or PSYC 227 Cognitive Psychology; Category 3 Developmental—PSYC 212 Psychology of Aging, PSYC 241 Developmental Psychology, PSYC 263 Child Psychology, or PSYC 347 Adolescent Psychology; Category 4 Socio-cultural Perspectives—PSYC 231 Multicultural Psychology, PSYC 239 Cross-Cultural Psychology, PSYC 307 Psychology of Yoga, PSYC 311 Psychology of Gender, PSYC 335 Sexualities and Gender Identities: LGBTQA+, or PSYC 349 Psychology of Women; Category 5 Clinical Perspectives—PSYC 314 Psychopathology, PSYC 321 Theories of Personality, or PSYC 357 Childhood Disorders; Category 6 Brain and Behavior—PSYC 310 Neuropsychology, PSYC 352 Behavioral Neuroscience, PSYC 353 Cognitive Neuroscience, or PSYC 355 Neuropsychopharmacology; Category 7 Fieldwork/Independent Research—PSYC 319, 320, 339, 358, 367, 368, or 472; Category 8 Capstone Seminar—PSYC 430–434, 436–440, 450, or 451. Also select 1 additional Psychology course. Career Pathways requirements list PATH 001 twice and PATH 003 [1].

Recommended plan [1] is for students admitted to the major in 2026–2027; another plan that year is Psychology/Teacher Education. Each semester totals 16 credits. Year 1 fall: INTD 101, Social Science Inquiry, PSYC 101, CRWT 102; spring: two General Education requirements, preferred MATH 108 Quantitative Reasoning, Category 1; PATH 001. Year 2 fall: General Education, Category 2, Category 3*, free elective; PATH 002. Spring: General Education, PSYC 242, Category 4, free elective; PATH 003. Year 3 fall: General Education, PSYC 303 (WI), PSYC 304, Psychology elective. Spring: Category 5 and three free electives. Year 4 fall: Category 6, Category 7 (Fieldwork, WI), two free electives. Spring: Category 8 Capstone Seminar (WI), three free electives. The plan lists PATH 001, PATH 002 and PATH 003; the requirements list PATH 001 twice and PATH 003 [1]. Plan total: 128 credits; GPA: 2.0 [1].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC101)

question: Are there any certificate programs undergrads can add on top of their major, like something in data analytics or business?

body.answer:
Yes. Undergraduates may pursue a minor or second major in addition to their degree program [4]. The catalog recognizes undergraduate certificates as a possible level of Academic Certificate, but does not say that students can add any certificate to their major [5][6]. It describes certificates as usually comprising credit-bearing courses, possibly with non-credit experiences; they are not graduation requirements and are removed from the degree audit [5][6].

For data analytics/business, the catalog lists the Business Analytics and Applied AI Minor, open to students in any major [1]. Requirements: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS, INFO 224 PRINCIPLES OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, INFO 310 BUSINESS ANALYTICS I, and INFO 345 AI FOR BUSINESS: HARNESSING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; plus 2 electives from ECON 310 ECONOMETRICS, INFO 233 INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING, INFO 311 BUSINESS ANALYTICS II, INFO 320 TOOLS FOR ANALYTICS AND AI, INFO 332 DATABASE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS, INFO 333 DATA VISUALIZATION, INFO 422 DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS, MGMT 373 MANAGEMENT SCIENCE, or MKTG 330 MARKETING RESEARCH [1]. It is a minor, not a certificate. The pages also list “Spanish for Healthcare and Human Services Professionals” as a new certificate, but do not identify it as data analytics/business [7].

For information about certificate offerings, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330; first floor of the Birch Mansion [5].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MN-BAAI) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/academics/)

question: My son wants to be a high school teacher. Does Ramapo offer a teacher certification, and does he have to major in education or in the subject he wants to teach?

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers teaching certification through its Teacher Education Program, approved by the New Jersey State Department of Education. [8]

For secondary education (such as high school), he should complete a primary major in the subject he wants to teach—for example, English, History or Mathematics—and apply to the Teacher Education Program for certification. He does not have to major in education for secondary certification. [8][9]

Ramapo’s only education degree is a BS in Elementary Education. Students pursuing that major must meet all Teacher Education Program requirements. [8][9]

Teacher Education applicants must have a GPA of 3.0 or higher and apply directly through the Teacher Education office. More information: https://www.ramapo.edu/te/ [8][9]

Sources: [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/)

question: is there a film or communication major? what would the first year look like

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo lists a Filmmaking BA (Bachelor of Arts) [1]. Its introductory courses are FILM 206 SOUND AND IMAGE; FILM 217 DIGITAL POST PRODUCTION; FILM 218 FUNDAMENTALS OF FILMMAKING; FILM 220 SCREENWRITING; THEA 217 VISUAL IMAGINATION; and THEA 220 INTRODUCTION TO ACTING [1]. Communication Arts is also described as a major, with a Digital Filmmaking concentration [10].

For first year, the pages describe First-Year Seminar (FYS), not a course-by-course major schedule. FYS courses focus on themes including Media & Communication; most are interdisciplinary, and class sizes are 20–25 [4]. Fall 2026 has 44 FYS courses [5]. Media & Communication options include “An Introduction to Modern-Day Journalism: Facts, Fiction and Everything In Between,” “The Ethics of Star Trek,” “Framing the World: Mobile Photography Between Art and Activism,” “Bollywood & Global Culture,” and “Writing Creatively with Social Media” [2]. Students are expected to read a common book selected by students, faculty, and staff during the summer before joining Ramapo [3].

The pages don’t give a specific first-year schedule for either major. First-year students are assigned professional advisors based on FYS selection; “Check your network in Connect to find your assigned academic advisor” [7]. Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207 [7].

question: Do AP credits count toward gen ed requirements? She has AP Calc and AP English Lang.

body.answer:
Yes, AP credit may count toward Gen Ed, but acceptance and applicability are evaluated; the pages don’t specify AP English Lang’s equivalency or Gen Ed application. [2][3][15]
For AP credit, students earning a 4 or 5 are eligible for course credit. Have College Board send official AP scores to Ramapo; after evaluation, a Transfer Credit Evaluation by email states accepted courses, credits, and Ramapo equivalents. [9] If she is a transfer applicant, submit an official score report to Admissions to have completed AP credit evaluated. [8]
For AP Calc, the result depends on the exam and score: AP Calculus AB score 4 or 5 earns Calculus I credit; AP Calculus BC score 4 or 5 earns Calculus I and II credit. [11][12][13] The catalog lists MATH 121 Calculus I as Gen Ed Quantitative Reasoning (GEQR), so accepted MATH 121 credit would match that category. [1] Pages don’t establish that her AP score will be awarded as MATH 121, or give the AP English Lang outcome; check her evaluation.
For questions about which Gen Ed requirements remain, academic advising can help: Center for Student Success, success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207. [17]

question: Which major would be better for getting into medical school, biology or biochemistry?

body.answer:
No page says that Biology or Biochemistry is better for medical-school admission, so I don’t have verified information to recommend one. Both are Bachelor of Science majors. Biology has a “Biology: General Pre-Med Track” plan; Biochemistry has a “Biochemistry/Pre-Medical Track” plan. [1][2]

The curricula differ: Biochemistry requires calculus I and II, physics with calculus, and a substantial chemistry sequence. Biology requires two math courses selected from its listed options, physics, and four electives, with options for its organic chemistry requirement. [1][2]

For help deciding, the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) recommends gathering information, reading the catalog, and talking with advisors and faculty. Contact: success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207. [3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BCHM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/)
